items.title: iOS placement lookup resolves successfully when the native SDK returns an error
items.body:
An iOS app cannot catch placement lookup failures: `getCurrentOfferingForPlacement()` resolves `undefined` even when the native SDK reports a connection error. `getOfferings()` correctly rejects the same failure.

## Reproduce

- Run [RCBugReporter](https://github.com/manyoneek/react-native-purchases/blob/95b8c71f100e35a4397906a9c414a3d89b09b0b0/qa/reproductions/2026-10-23/rn-placement-error/source.zip) and tap **Network error case**. This sends real SDK requests to a closed localhost port.
- `getOfferings()` rejects with code 33, but `getCurrentOfferingForPlacement()` resolves `undefined`. Both should reject.

Reproduced October 23: SDK 10.15.1 (`bde1095e8411`), RN 0.87.1, shared SDK 19.15.1, RevenueCat 5.98.0, iOS 27.1 simulator.

[Fix, tests and before/after demo](https://github.com/RevenueCat/react-native-purchases/pull/2054).

items.title: Reject native errors from iOS placement lookup
items.body:
Use the existing error-aware completion helper for iOS placement lookup. Native failures now reject the JavaScript promise; successful results are unchanged. Fixes #2053. ## Reproduce - Run [RCBugReporter](https://github.com/manyoneek/react-native-purchases/blob/95b8c71f100e35a4397906a9c414a3d89b09b0b0/qa/reproductions/2026-10-23/rn-placement-error/source.zip) and tap **Network error case**. This sends real SDK requests to a closed localhost port. - `getOfferings()` rejects with code 33, but `getCurrentOfferingForPlacement()` resolves `undefined`. Both should reject. - Apply the fix and repeat; then relaunch and run **Online control** to check a successful Test Store lookup. ## Checked - Native XCTest: 1 failure before; all 4 cases pass after. Checks error details, placement forwarding and successful results. - Same iOS app: 1 failure before; both checks pass after. The failed request reaches `catch`; the online control still returns an offering. - 274 core and 37 UI tests, build and typecheck pass. The unit case uses network error 10; the real blocked-endpoint request returns code 33. Hosted CI completion is unverified. Android and physical devices were not tested. Test command (after installing the example pods; select an installed simulator): ```sh xcodebuild test -workspace examples/purchaseTesterTypescript/ios/PurchaseTester.xcworkspace -scheme RNPurchases-Unit-UnitTests -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone Duo' -configuration Release CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO ``` Tested October 23: SDK 10.15.1 (`bde1095e8411`), RN 0.87.1, shared SDK 19.15.1, RevenueCat 5.98.0, iOS 27.1 simulator. Test app: **RCBugReporter**, [SDK Bug Reporter](https://app.revenuecat.com/projects/602cc762/apps/app4ca00b430f), project `proj602cc762`, Test Store app `app4ca00b430f`. Present since [#938](https://github.com/RevenueCat/react-native-purchases/pull/938), incorporating [#925](https://github.com/RevenueCat/react-native-purchases/pull/925), `a3d1f06386a6` (March 13, 2024), first release **7.24.0**. Historical bridge tests confirmed it; no full historical app run. ## Before → after

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11eb0b40-0f8f-4037-9cfa-907230bad941 [Source, logs and recordings](https://github.com/manyoneek/react-native-purchases/tree/95b8c71f100e35a4397906a9c414a3d89b09b0b0/qa/reproductions/2026-10-23/rn-placement-error)

items.title: iOS: EXC_BAD_ACCESS in `Offerings.offering(identifier:)` when `RevenueCatUI.Paywall` options include an offering
items.body:
- [ ] I have updated Purchases SDK to the latest version (we're on 10.4.2; the code paths below are unchanged in 10.12.2 and purchases-ios 5.94.0)
- [x] I have read the [Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/RevenueCat/react-native-purchases/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have searched the [Community](https://community.revenuecat.com)
- [x] I have read [docs.revenuecat.com](https://docs.revenuecat.com/)
- [x] I have searched for [existing Github issues](https://github.com/RevenueCat/react-native-purchases/issues)

**Describe the bug**

On iOS, `<RevenueCatUI.Paywall>` sometimes crashes with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` (`KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS` at `0x0`) inside RevenueCatUI while it resolves the offering passed in `options.offering`. The crashing thread is hashing the offering identifier for the `Offerings.all` lookup, and the `NSString` behind that identifier appears to have been freed already.

It's rare and only in production: 6 crashes from 6 users since Sept 26. Every one happened 0.3–2.3 s after the paywall screen opened right after sign-in, 40–400 ms after a fresh offerings response, while another thread was caching offerings (`DeviceCache.cache(offerings:)`), warming the paywall cache, or checking fonts.

1. Environment
   1. Platform: iOS
   2. SDK version: react-native-purchases and react-native-purchases-ui 10.4.2 (PurchasesHybridCommon/PurchasesHybridCommonUI 18.19.0, RevenueCat/RevenueCatUI 5.80.2)
   3. OS version: iOS 26.4.2 to 26.7 (iPhone12,8, iPhone14,3, iPhone14,5, iPhone15,3, iPhone17,1 and one more)
   4. Xcode/Android Studio version: Xcode 26.6
   5. React Native version: 0.87.1 (New Architecture, Hermes)
   6. SDK installation (CocoaPods + version or manual): CocoaPods 1.16.2
   7. How widespread is the issue. Percentage of devices affected: well under 1% of iOS users who open the paywall (6 users so far)
2. [Debug logs](https://docs.revenuecat.com/docs/debugging) that reproduce the issue

   We don't have verbose logs from an affected device. These are the RevenueCat console lines our crash reporter captured before one of the crashes (t = paywall screen opened; offering ids redacted):

   ```
   t+0.26s  [RevenueCat] Could not find default package for paywall. Using first package instead. ...
   t+0.55s  [RevenueCat] Mapping for '' could not be found. Falling back to system font.
   t+0.68s  [RevenueCat] Could not find default package for paywall. Using first package instead. ...
   t+1.03s  [RevenueCat] Could not find default package for paywall. Using first package instead. ...
   t+1.09s  [RevenueCat] ⚠️ There's a problem with your configuration. No packages could be found for offering with identifier <id>. ... (one line per offering)
   t+1.19s  (the same batch of offering warnings again)
   t+1.25s  EXC_BAD_ACCESS
   ```

   We read the repeated "default package" lines as the paywall being rebuilt as `options` changed (see below).
3. Steps to reproduce, with a description of expected vs. actual behavior

   We haven't reproduced it locally; it looks timing-dependent. The production pattern:

   1. Configure Purchases with `purchasesAreCompletedBy: MY_APP`, sign in, and open the paywall screen while offerings are being refreshed.
   2. Fetch `Purchases.getOfferings()` and render the current offering:

      ```tsx
      <RevenueCatUI.Paywall
        options={{
          offering, // offerings.current
          displayCloseButton: false,
          customVariables: {
            has_expired_subscription: CustomVariableValue.boolean(hasExpiredSubscription),
            has_introductory_offer: CustomVariableValue.boolean(hasIntroductoryOffer),
          },
        }}
        purchaseLogic={purchaseLogic}
      />
      ```

   3. Shortly after mount, re-render with a new `options` object because the custom-variable inputs finished loading. Each re-send makes `PaywallViewWrapper -setOptions:` call `updateWithOfferingIdentifier:presentedOfferingContext:` again with the same offering.

   **Expected:** the paywall loads (or reloads) without crashing.
   **Actual:** occasionally `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` in `Offerings.offering(identifier:)`.
4. **Other information** (e.g. stacktraces, related issues, suggestions how to fix, links for us to have context, eg. stackoverflow, etc.)

   Crashing thread:

   ```
   0  libobjc.A.dylib     _lookUpImpOrForward
   1  libobjc.A.dylib     __objc_msgSend_uncached
   2  libswiftCore.dylib  _StringObject.sharedUTF8.getter
   3  libswiftCore.dylib  String.hash(into:)
   4                      protocol witness for Hashable._rawHashValue(seed:) in conformance String
   5                      specialized __RawDictionaryStorage.find<A>(_:)
   6                      specialized Dictionary.subscript.getter
   7  RevenueCat          Offerings.offering(identifier:)                                       Offerings.swift:106
   8  RevenueCatUI        PurchaseHandler.resolvePaywallViewData(for:workflowsEndpointEnabled:)  PurchaseHandler.swift:471
   ```

   Another thread at the same moment, caching the offerings response:

   ```
   SynchronizedLargeItemCache.getFileURL(for:)                                         SynchronizedLargeItemCache.swift:57
   DeviceCache.cache(offerings:preferredLocales:appUserID:)                            DeviceCache.swift:226
   closure #1 in OfferingsManager.handleOfferingsBackendResult(...)                    OfferingsManager.swift:328
   closure #1 in OfferingsManager.createOfferings(from:loadedFromDiskCache:fetchPolicy:completion:)  OfferingsManager.swift:305
   CachingProductsManager.products(withIdentifiers:completion:)                       CachingProductsManager.swift:68
   OfferingsManager.fetchProducts(withIdentifiers:fromResponse:completion:)            OfferingsManager.swift:415
   OfferingsManager.handleOfferingsBackendResult(...)                                  OfferingsManager.swift:323
   closure #1 in closure #2 in GetOfferingsOperation.getOfferings(completion:)         GetOfferingsOperation.swift:75
   HTTPClient.handle(urlResponse:request:urlRequest:data:error:requestStartTime:)      HTTPClient.swift:557
   ```

   A third thread was in `DefaultPaywallFontsManager.fontIsAlreadyInstalled(fontName:fontFamily:)` (`PaywallFontManagerType.swift:123`).

   **What we think is happening (not confirmed):**

   - The string being hashed is the identifier RNPaywalls passes from `options.offering.identifier`: `-applyNonCustomVariableOptionsFromPendingOptions` → `-[RCPaywallViewController updateWithOfferingIdentifier:presentedOfferingContext:]`. Hashing goes through `_StringObject.sharedUTF8` and `objc_msgSend`, so it's a bridged `NSString`, and the message send lands on a dead object.
   - Once the view is in the hierarchy, `setOptions:` re-applies the offering on every options update, even when the offering hasn't changed. Each call sets `configuration.content`, whose `didSet` replaces the hosting controller and starts a new load.
   - `viewDidLoad` also starts `prefetchExitOffer()`, which calls `resolveOffering(for: self.configuration.content)` (the workflows endpoint is off by default in 5.80.2). Both that and `PaywallView.loadPaywallData()` reach `resolvePaywallViewData(for:workflowsEndpointEnabled:)`, which awaits `purchases.offerings()` and then calls `offerings.offering(identifier:)`.
   - So a resolve for the previous content can still be suspended in `purchases.offerings()` when the main thread replaces `configuration.content`. When the offerings response lands (second stack above), it resumes and hashes an identifier whose backing string has been released. The async stack ends at `resolvePaywallViewData`, so we can't tell which caller it was.
   - Toolchain: the first crash came in our first release built with Xcode 26.6 (crash reports show `clang-2100.1.1.101`). Earlier releases were built with Xcode 26.1.1 (`clang-1700.4.4.1`), had the same RevenueCat versions and paywall code, and had no occurrences. That's only a correlation, but it means a compiler-side lifetime change is possible.

   **Latest versions:** purchases-ios 5.94.0 still resolves `.offeringIdentifier` through `offerings.offering(identifier:)` in `PurchaseHandler`, and `PaywallViewWrapper.m` in react-native-purchases-ui 10.12.2 has the same `setOptions:` / `updateWithOfferingIdentifier:` logic (it only adds the new event callbacks). We haven't run those versions in production.

   **Possible fixes:**

   - In `PaywallViewWrapper`, skip `updateWithOfferingIdentifier:` when the offering identifier and presented offering context haven't changed. Unrelated option updates, such as custom variables, which iOS ignores after the first layout anyway, then wouldn't rebuild the paywall.
   - In RevenueCatUI, make sure an in-flight resolve owns its content and identifier, or is cancelled, when `configuration.content` is replaced.

   **Our workaround:** we only ever show the current offering, so we stopped passing `options.offering` (the native paywall then resolves `.defaultOffering`), and we keep `options` fixed after mount so `setOptions:` isn't re-sent. We'll report back if the crash stops once that ships.

**Additional context**

No Android equivalent in our crash reports. The crashing frames are in purchases-ios (RevenueCatUI), but we only hit them through the react-native-purchases-ui `Paywall` component, so we're filing here. Feel free to move it.

I am using the `RevenueCatUI.Paywall` component on a route. On iOS, it correctly displays my only template configured on my RC's project. However, on Android, it displays the default template.

Apparently, from the logs:

```
Could not process value for variable 'sub_offer_duration' for package 'my_package_name'. Please check that the product for that package matches the requirements for that variable. Defaulting to empty string.
```

I am not rendering the `sub_offer_duration` in my template.

   1. Platform: Android
   2. SDK version: 8.5.3
   3. OS version: Android 14
   4. Xcode/Android Studio version:
   5. React Native version: 0.74.5

items.body:
Based on PHC PR https://github.com/RevenueCat/purchases-hybrid-common/pull/1665.

## API

We will now send the `presentedOfferingContext` from the passed `Offering` along with the event. This PR adds the new API variant that takes an `Offering` instead of a plain string `offeringId`. The latter is now deprecated in favor of this new API variant. We will derive the `presentedOfferingContext` from this `Offering` and send it along with the request.

```
await Purchases.trackCustomPaywallImpression({ paywallId: "", offering })
```

---

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes analytics event shape and bridge null-handling for paywall impressions; backward compatible via deprecated `offeringId` but incorrect offering/package data could skew placement analytics.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Custom paywall impression tracking** now accepts a `PurchasesOffering` via `trackCustomPaywallImpression({ offering, paywallId })`. The JS layer derives `offeringId` and `presentedOfferingContext` from the offering’s first available package (placement/targeting), prefers that over legacy `offeringId`, and always forwards a normalized native payload with explicit `null` fields.
> 
> **Native bridges** strip nulls before hybrid common on Android (`mapWithoutNullValues`, also reused for `setAppstackAttributionParams`) and map `NSNull` to omitted keys on iOS for this call. items.title: feat(ads): admob adapter
items.body:
## Description

Adds `react-native-purchases-admob`, a new automatic ad tracking package covering the 3rd party `react-native-google-mobile-ads` package. This is the most commonly used admob package available for admob

The `adsTester` example changes that exercise it are in the stacked PR.

## Changes

### Adapter
- `RevenueCatAdMob.create{Interstitial,AppOpen,Rewarded,RewardedInterstitial}Ad(adUnitId, options)` creates the ad and tracks loaded, failed-to-load, displayed, opened and revenue.
- `trackAd(ad, options)` does the same for an ad the app created.
- `showAndTrack(ad, { placement })` for show-time placement overrides.
- `useTrackingBannerAdProps(...)` (hook) / `trackingBannerAdProps(...)` for `<BannerAd>`, `trackNativeAd(nativeAd)` for native ads, `impressionIdOf(ad)`.
- Reward verification: `createRewardedAd(id, { enableRewardVerification: true })` attaches the token as SSV options at creation. The library only accepts them there. `showWithRewardVerification(ad, callbacks)` polls and returns a `VerifiedReward`.
- Events are stamped with `AdCaptureMethod.reactNativeAdMobAdapter`.

### Example usage

```tsx
import { RevenueCatAdMob, useTrackingBannerAdProps } from 'react-native-purchases-admob';

const rewarded = await RevenueCatAdMob.createRewardedAd(adUnitId, {
  placement: 'level_complete',
  enableRewardVerification: true,
});
rewarded.load();
await RevenueCatAdMob.showWithRewardVerification(rewarded, {
  onRewardVerificationCompleted: result => grant(result),
});

function HomeBanner() {
  const props = useTrackingBannerAdProps({ unitId, size: BannerAdSize.BANNER, placement: 'home_bottom' });
  return <BannerAd {...props} />;
}
```

### Why 17.x
17.0.0 added `ResponseInfo` on loaded events, the `IMPRESSION` event, `PaidEvent.valueMicros` and `error.reason`.

The adapter needs all four. Verified on 17.0.0, 17.1.0 and 17.2.0.

The only exception is rewarded ad ssv, where we are using our custom impression id, because it is not available properly yet in the API. We might change it in the future.

### Core SDK
- added an optional `captureMethod` so the new adapter can pass in the new capture method type

### Examples
- `adsTester` rewritten to use the adapter in the stacked PR

### Release wiring
- Fastfile: adapter in the version-bump map, fourth `npm publish` in `release`.
- CircleCI: prepare, API tests and unit tests for the adapter in `analyse_js`.
- Repo-wide `tslint` already crashes on `main` under TypeScript 5.4.5; not addressed.

## Tests
- unit tests, api tests
- full e2e simulator test with all ad formats, against production system, both with android and ios builds, using the `adsTester` from the stacked PR
- full e2e for manual integration to catch regression issues

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New monetization surface (ad events and server-side reward verification) with complex lifecycle edge cases, though failures are mostly logged and tracking calls are non-throwing.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **`react-native-purchases-admob`**, a new workspace package that bridges **`react-native-google-mobile-ads` (17+)** to RevenueCat’s `Purchases.adTracker` and reward-verification APIs.
> 
> The **`RevenueCatAdMob`** API replaces or wraps ad creation (`createInterstitialAd`, `createAppOpenAd`, async rewarded variants), attaches listeners for load/display/revenue/failure events, and forwards them with placement overrides and **`AdCaptureMethod.reactNativeAdMobAdapter`**. Banners use **`useTrackingBannerAdProps`** / **`trackingBannerAdProps`**; native ads use **`trackNativeAd`**. Optional **`enableRewardVerification`** pins a pre-request impression id, injects AdMob SSV options, blocks unsafe reloads, and **`showWithRewardVerification`** polls RevenueCat after the user earns a reward.
> 
> **Core `react-native-purchases`** gains **`AdCaptureMethod`** and an optional **`captureMethod`** on ad tracking / reward metadata types (marked `@internal` for official adapters).
> 
> **Release and CI**: the adapter is added to yarn workspaces, root publish exclusions, Jest ignore paths, CircleCI prepare/API/unit steps, and Fastlane version bumps plus a fourth **`npm publish`** in the release lane.
>
